thread:
Sarah: quick question — thinking about on‑prem upgrade UX: can we move to an "isolated registry layering" approach where we stream content in chunked layers to a local registry and verify signatures per-chunk on apply rather than verifying entire bundles up-front?

Raj: idea being each layer is a content-addressed chunk set with its own signature + a signed manifest describing ordering and compatibility. verify-on-apply would mean smaller memory footprint but more complex failure semantics. :thinking:

Mike: tradeoffs: verify-on-pull (verify before storing) = safer, simpler rollback because store only valid bits. But with large corp networks and slow links, we pay big temp-storage cost and double IO. verify-on-apply (store then verify on activation) reduces upfront stalls but you need atomic activation and a scan/repair path.

Tanya: security note — we must ensure operator can't accidentally activate a chunk that fails verify. So activation must be gated by a verification pass that can abort and leave system in previous active state. HSM/KMS calls should sign activation receipts.

Sarah: do folks prefer a layered layout that allows partial resume? Example: chunk-0001, chunk-0002... apply pointer moves when verified. So if transfer fails we resume from last verified chunk.

Raj: yes, resume-by-chunk is nice. Also allows dedup across releases if chunks are content-addressed. But chunk boundary choice matters — too small = many signatures and overhead; too big = large retransfer on minor delta. Consider variable chunking (content-defined) with a target avg size (e.g., 16MB).

Mike: implementation sketch: local registry implements two stores: staging (untrusted) and active (trusted). Staging receives blobs via transfer protocol (rsync/OCI/p2p). After transfer we run a verifier worker that checks chunk signatures and writes verified blobs to active immutables. Activation is an atomic swap of the active manifest symlink.

Oliver: what about streaming verification during transfer? We could verify chunk as it arrives (stream-verify) and mark chunk as verified without fully writing twice. That helps with disk IO. But needs careful partial-write handling and restarted checks.

Raj: streaming-verify + content-defined chunking feels right. Need a robust checksumming + signature chain: chunk_i signed by pack-signer, and manifest signs sequence + compatibility metadata + mutability markers.

Tanya: audit trails required — ops must be able to show which key signed which chunk and when activation happened. Add activation receipts and a verification log stored in the control-plane events.

Sarah: UX: operator CLI should expose small commands:

```
# push artifact archive to local gateway and stage
rwr push --target gateway.local:8443 --chunk-size=16MB ./release-v1.tar
# verify staged and promote to active (idempotent)
rwr promote --artifact release-v1 --verify-mode=stream-then-commit
```

Mike: fallback / safety nets: we need automatic revert window where new active is staged but traffic routed to previous version until health-checks pass. Canary behavior for on-prem: route X% of local requests to new image then ramp. We already have routing infra in dedicated but need lightweight operator toggles here.

Raj: garbage collection concerns: if staging holds partial chunks and active holds verified blobs, GC must not remove shared blobs referenced by older actives. Keep a simple refcount store metadata and epoch-based tombstones.

Tanya: encryption-in-transit and at-rest — staging blobs should be encrypted with cluster key that the verifier can decrypt when checking. Keys stored in operator KMS; HSM ok. Also pin algorithm versions in manifest so future verifiers reject old weak sigs.

Oliver: CI integration: release pipeline should produce chunk-level signatures and manifest. We should publish a verifier binary with stable ABI so on-prem can run the same verification code we run in CI. Also add a small attest bundle that contains verifier hash signed by our release key.

Sarah: other failure modes: partial verify that later fails mid-activation. Proposal: activation uses a two-phase commit: 1) verifier marks all required blobs verified and creates activation txn 2) apply switchpoint updates active pointer 3) post-apply sanity checks — if any fail, rollback to previous pointer and emit remediation tasks.

Mike: ops automation: include a 'repair' command which re-fetches missing blobs from other nodes or from offline seed medium. For fully air-gapped sites, seed devices must carry missing chunk indexes and signatures.

Raj: long-term refactor: consider moving from a monolithic bundle format to a delta-layered registry that supports branching (A/B content-addressed trees). That simplifies rollouts and dedup but is more stateful.

Tanya: compliance: ensure retention of verification logs for N days, and provide exportable signed manifests for audits.

Sarah: OK next steps: Raj/Mike to draft a short RFC with implementation sketch (staging vs active stores, chunking strategy, verification chain, activation protocol). Tanya add security checklist and log schema. Oliver draft verifier distribution and CI contract. I'll coordinate. :thumbsup:

OpsBot: deploy-check: no active deploys running on cluster 'onprem-west-3'. All gates clear.

Mike: will sketch proto this week, aim to demo chunk resume + atomic activation in next arch sync.

Raj: one more note — measure CPU costs of streaming verification vs post-verify. We'll add microbench marks to RFC.

Sarah: thanks — filing RFC draft by EOW.
